```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Support for a mass working-class party that contests elections and builds movements.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Such a party must be born out of a level of class struggle and unity far greater than exists today.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Until such a time arrives, DSA is seen as a pre-party organization, one of many groups working to develop the forces necessary to build such a party.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Support for an oppositional electoral strategy that remains completely independent from the Democratic Party apparatus.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Such a strategy must reject the idea that socialists can capture the Democratic Party and instead seek to break unions and social movements from their current dependence on the Democratic Party establishment.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Tactical flexibility is possible on the question of what ballot line socialists run on.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"It makes sense for DSA to endorse class struggle candidates who are not socialists but whose campaigns advance key parts of the DSA platform in certain cases.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Such campaigns can help build class consciousness and polarize (and eventually split) the Democratic Party coalition.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Candidates running as socialists should serve the movement, not the other way around.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Socialist politicians should act as organizers for the socialist movement and as popularizers of DSA ideas first, and as legislators second.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
